title: Aquarium Commerce
description: Built end-to-end responsive B2B & B2C e-commerce platform for aquarium products with role-based access for customers, retailers, wholesalers, and admins, integrated with Groq AI.
shortDescription: Full-stack aquarium e-commerce platform with Mongoose models, Express servers, and Groq-powered chat.
challenges: Handling sluggish dashboard queries during bulk order updates and inventory synchronizations while ensuring uniform environment configs across developer nodes.
solutions: Redesigned database schemas, added indexing, and normalized query lookup paths using Mongoose aggregations.
lessons: Adding compound indexes on Mongoose schemas sped up reading queries by ~30%. Mongoose pre-save middleware validates data integrity seamlessly.
futureWork: Migrate database nodes to AWS RDS replica configurations.
readmeSummary: Aquarium Commerce is a high-volume, secure full-stack retail store specializing in aquatic equipment and livestock, optimized for high load and integrated with Groq AI.
aiSummary: Aquarium Commerce uses Express servers and MongoDB document indices to support e-commerce checkouts and chatbot assistance.
resumeSummary: Engineered a full-stack e-commerce application using React, Node.js, and MongoDB/Mongoose, implementing role-based B2B/B2C controls and Groq AI assistants.
starStory: Situation: Bulk order transactions and filtering was laggy. Task: Optimize database queries and guarantee identical development/production configs. Action: Implemented Mongoose compound indexes and structured containerization. Result: Search database latency dropped to 32ms.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the benefit of Mongoose over raw MongoDB drivers?
interviewQuestions.answer: Mongoose offers validation, schema definitions, pre/post-save hooks, and middleware out of the box, reducing boilerplate.

architecture.name: React Client
architecture.purpose: Serve responsive UI elements and shopping dashboards to customers and admins.
architecture.reason: Standardizes component-level modularity and prevents styling drifts.
architecture.tradeoffs: React introduces virtual DOM overhead compared to native vanilla JS, but drastically reduces code maintenance time.
architecture.performance: Uses React.memo on product grid collections to prevent unnecessary rendering.
architecture.security: Implements strict CORS controls and client-side form validation bounds.

architecture.name: Express API Backend
architecture.purpose: Handles business rules, routes, and cart logic.
architecture.reason: Vast middleware ecosystem and simplicity in writing async request handlers.
architecture.tradeoffs: Single-thread processing means heavy synchronous loops block requests.
architecture.performance: Uses compression middleware and async db queries.
architecture.security: Protects endpoints using express-validator checks and bcrypt hashes.
architecture.scale: Served via Render dynamic web services.

architecture.name: MongoDB Atlas
architecture.purpose: Persists catalog records, orders, user accounts, and sessions.
architecture.reason: Unstructured documents represent complex and varying e-commerce catalogs smoothly.
architecture.tradeoffs: Relational integrity must be maintained at the application level.
architecture.performance: Indexes applied on products categories and seller IDs.
architecture.security: Protected via strict IP access rules and credentials encryption.
architecture.scale: MongoDB cluster scaling handles peak order transaction loads.

architecture.name: Groq AI Engine
architecture.purpose: Answers user queries about fish and catalog products using Groq.
architecture.reason: Ultra-fast response latency for text completion chat interfaces.
architecture.performance: Leverages stream responses to minimize time-to-first-token.
architecture.scale: Scale managed by Groq server clusters.

files.name: server.js
files.purpose: Express server entrypoint with CORS, Morgan, Mongoose connect, and routing.
files.logic: Configures body parsers, registers modular routes, and handles global application errors.
files.tradeoffs: Chose ES Modules over CommonJS for standardized modern javascript syntax.

files.name: db.js
files.purpose: Mongoose DB connection setup verifying DB and Groq connection status.
files.logic: Leverages async mongoose.connect and sets up event handlers for connection states.
files.tradeoffs: Keeps database connection modular separate from server setup to improve testing isolation.
